user_text: Summarize the benefits of code review for a small team.
assistant_text:
# Benefits of Code Review for a Small Team

## Quality & Reliability
- **Catches bugs early** before they reach production
- **Enforces coding standards** and consistency across the codebase
- **Reduces technical debt** by encouraging cleaner solutions upfront

## Knowledge Sharing
- **Spreads context** so no single person is the only one who understands a feature
- **Onboards new members faster** by exposing them to existing patterns
- **Surfaces better approaches** team members may not have considered

## Team Collaboration
- **Builds shared ownership** — everyone feels responsible for the codebase
- **Encourages communication** and constructive feedback habits
- **Reduces bus factor** (risk of losing critical knowledge if someone leaves)

## Long-Term Efficiency
- **Fewer production incidents** mean less time firefighting
- **Easier maintenance** when code is readable and well-structured
- **Documents decisions** through review comments and discussions

---

## Practical Tips for Small Teams
- Keep reviews **focused and timely** (avoid large, delayed PRs)
- Use a **lightweight process** — don't over-engineer it
- Treat feedback as **collaborative, not critical**

> Even a quick second set of eyes can prevent costly mistakes and keep a small team aligned.
Code review helps small teams catch bugs early, share knowledge, and maintain a consistent, high-quality codebase.

1. **Bug detection** — A second set of eyes catches mistakes before they reach production.
2. **Knowledge sharing** — Team members learn from each other's code, reducing reliance on any single person.
Code review builds a culture of **shared ownership**, where everyone feels collectively responsible for the quality of the codebase rather than protective of their individual work.

user_text: State one risk if reviews are skipped.
assistant_text: If reviews are skipped, **technical debt accumulates rapidly**, as unchecked code tends to be inconsistent and harder to maintain over time.
Track **defect escape rate** — the number of bugs found in production versus those caught during review — to measure how effectively your review process is preventing issues from reaching users.
A consistent code review practice is one of the simplest investments a small team can make for long-term code health and team cohesion.

• Code review is a simple but powerful practice for small teams.
• It improves quality, sharing knowledge, and team collaboration.
• Skipping it leads to bugs, debt, and siloed knowledge.
• Tracking metrics like defect escape rate shows its real impact.
• Even a lightweight process delivers significant long-term benefits.
Code review is a small investment that pays off in fewer bugs, stronger teams, and a healthier codebase.
Code review is only effective if feedback is timely and constructive — slow or overly critical reviews can bottleneck progress and harm team morale.
Done poorly, code review can slow teams and hurt morale.
Code review boosts quality and collaboration, but only works well when kept timely, constructive, and lightweight.
